Yes; A's earliest being smaller is enough.
Yes; B's latest being larger is enough.
No; TrueTime never supports any ordering.
why: TrueTime 的安全判断是 A_latest < B_earliest。这里只是 108 和 105 重叠，所以系统不能用时间证明先后。
why_en: The safe TrueTime rule is A_latest < B_earliest, and overlapping intervals do not prove order.
tradeoff: 安全排序断言 vs 不确定区间等待
optionExplanations: 安全的前提是 A 的区间必须完全落在 B 之前、不能有任何重叠；这里 108 和 105 重叠，真实发生时间完全可能是 B 先于 A。
误解：只看 A 的 earliest 更小不够，A 的真实时间点可能落在区间任何位置，包括比 B 晚。
误解：B 的 latest 更大同样不能证明顺序，两个区间只要重叠，谁先谁后都有可能。
误解：区间不重叠时 TrueTime 完全能安全断言顺序，只是这个具体例子恰好重叠了。
optionExplanations_en: The safe rule is A.latest < B.earliest; here 108 and 105 overlap, so the true instants could just as easily put B before A.
Misconception: A's earliest being smaller isn't enough -- A's true instant could fall anywhere in its interval, including after B.
Misconception: B's latest being larger doesn't prove order either -- with overlapping intervals, either event could truly come first.
Misconception: TrueTime can safely assert order whenever intervals don't overlap; this example just happens to overlap.

scenario: 团队想用 Spanner 里单行 read-modify-write 生成严格全局递增序列，所有业务事件都必须排成一个总序。
scenario_en: A team wants to use a single-row read-modify-write in Spanner to generate a strictly globally increasing sequence for all business events.
q: 严格全局顺序的成本是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of strict global ordering?
options: 中心化更新会成为吞吐瓶颈，可能只有百 ops/s 量级
它会让所有写入自动分散到无限多热点
它比本地 Snowflake 更高可用且无任何等待
它会把 64-bit ID 空间缩小到 10 个值
options_en: The centralized update becomes a throughput bottleneck, potentially around hundreds of ops per second.
It automatically spreads every write across infinitely many hotspots.
It is more available than local Snowflake and needs no waiting.
It shrinks the 64-bit ID space to 10 values.
why: 严格总序通常要把所有事件挤过同一个协调点或同一行状态。放松为大致时间顺序或只保留必要因果，吞吐会高很多。
why_en: Strict global order usually funnels events through one coordination point, so relaxing order can dramatically improve throughput.
tradeoff: 严格总序 vs 发号吞吐
optionExplanations: 所有事件都挤过同一行 read-modify-write，串行更新的上限通常只有百级 ops/s，远撑不住高并发发号。
误解：单行更新恰恰是把所有写入收拢到一处，而不是分散到热点，这跟分片扩展是反方向。
误解：单行成为全局瓶颈，可用性和等待时间都会比本地发号的 Snowflake 差，不是更好。
误解：ID 空间的位宽和这行计数器的更新方式无关，不会被压缩到 10 个值。
optionExplanations_en: Funneling every event through one row's read-modify-write typically caps throughput at only hundreds of ops per second, far short of high-concurrency issuance.
Misconception: a single-row update concentrates writes into one place rather than spreading them across hotspots -- the opposite of sharded scaling.
Misconception: that single row becomes a global bottleneck, so availability and latency are worse than local Snowflake issuance, not better.
Misconception: the bit width of the ID space has nothing to do with how this counter row is updated, so it isn't squeezed down to 10 values.

scenario: 分布式数据库按主键范围分片。你使用严格递增 ID，所有新写入都落在当前最大 ID 附近。
scenario_en: A distributed database shards by primary-key range. You use strictly increasing IDs, so every new write lands near the current maximum ID.
q: 单调递增 ID 会带来什么风险？
q_en: What risk do monotonically increasing IDs create?
options: 新写入集中到最后一个 range，形成写热点
每个 range 收到的写入量都会天然保持完全均匀
ID 越大，value 会自动变小
数据库不再需要复制
options_en: New writes concentrate on the last range and create a write hotspot.
Every range naturally receives a perfectly even amount of writes.
The larger the ID, the smaller the value becomes.
The database no longer needs replication.
why: 范围分片看的是 key 的位置，递增 ID 会让最新写入总追着尾部 range 跑。可以用打散位、预分裂或非严格顺序方案缓解。
why_en: Range sharding sends increasing IDs to the tail range, creating a write hotspot unless the keyspace is spread out.
tradeoff: 按 ID 扫描友好 vs 写入均衡
optionExplanations: 范围分片按 key 大小切段，严格递增 ID 会让每次新写入都落进当前最大的那个 range，写压力全堆在尾部。
误解：递增 ID 恰恰相反，会让写入越来越偏向最后一个 range，完全谈不上天然均匀。
误解：ID 大小和 value 内容大小没有任何关系，这是两个独立的维度。
误解：分片策略跟是否需要复制无关，复制仍然是保证容错的独立机制。
optionExplanations_en: Range sharding cuts the keyspace by value, so strictly increasing IDs push every new write into whichever range currently holds the max, piling pressure on the tail.
Misconception: increasing IDs do the opposite of balancing -- they skew writes more and more toward the last range over time.
Misconception: the size of the ID has no bearing on the size of the value; those are unrelated dimensions.
Misconception: the sharding strategy is independent of replication, which remains a separate mechanism for fault tolerance.

scenario: 为每天 100 亿条订单发号：ID 要进 MySQL 主键索引，并支持按时间范围扫描。
scenario_en: You are issuing IDs for ten billion orders a day; the ID goes into a MySQL primary-key index and must support time-range scans.
q: 选择分布式 ID 方案时通常要同时检查哪些维度？
q_en: Which dimensions should you check when choosing a distributed ID scheme?
options: 唯一性：重复 ID 会造成支付、主键或追踪错误
紧凑性：大 key 会增加索引和存储成本
顺序语义：是否需要时间排序或因果排序
颜色语义：ID 字符串是否看起来更美观
options_en: Uniqueness: duplicate IDs can break payments, primary keys, or tracing.
Compactness: large keys increase index and storage cost.
Ordering semantics: whether time order or causal order is required.
Color semantics: whether the ID string looks visually nicer.
why: ID 不是只要“不重复”就结束，还会影响索引大小、写热点、范围扫描和调试链路。外观美观不是系统设计约束。
why_en: ID design affects uniqueness, index cost, hotspots, scans, and tracing, not just whether the string looks nice.
optionExplanations: 重复 ID 一旦流进支付、主键或分布式追踪，后果是错账、覆盖数据或链路断裂，这条挡住的是正确性风险。
ID 越长，索引和存储的膨胀就越明显，紧凑性挡住的是长期的存储成本压力。
有些下游要按时间扫描或要保住 happened-before，顺序语义没考虑清楚，后续排序或因果判断就无从下手。
ID 字符串好不好看不是系统设计约束，选型时不该把这条当作评估维度。
optionExplanations_en: Duplicate IDs flowing into payments, primary keys, or tracing cause wrong charges, overwritten data, or broken traces -- this dimension guards correctness.
The longer the ID, the more index and storage bloat you carry, so compactness guards against long-term storage cost pressure.
Some downstream needs range scans by time or must preserve happened-before, so skipping ordering semantics leaves later sorting or causal checks with nothing to work from.
How visually appealing an ID string looks isn't a system-design constraint and shouldn't factor into the choice.
